skills.name: Mode, mean and median of raw data

note.text:
Measures of central tendency give one typical value of the data.
• Mode: the value that occurs most often (there may be no mode, or more than one).
• Mean: the sum of the values ÷ the number of values.
• Median: the middle value when the data are arranged in order. If there is an even number of values, the median is halfway between the two middle values.
Example: 3, 7, 2, 7, 6 → in order 2, 3, 6, 7, 7: mode 7; mean (3 + 7 + 2 + 7 + 6) ÷ 5 = 25 ÷ 5 = 5; median 6.
The range (largest − smallest) shows how spread out the data are.

worked_example.problem: Find the mode, mean and median of {a}, {b}, {c}, {d}, {e}.
steps: In order: {listStr(sorted([a, b, c, d, e]))}. Mode: {modeOf([a, b, c, d, e])}.
Mean: {sum([a, b, c, d, e])} ÷ {5} = {meanOf([a, b, c, d, e])}. Median: the middle value, {medianOf([a, b, c, d, e])}.
worked_example.answer: mode {modeOf([a, b, c, d, e])}, mean {meanOf([a, b, c, d, e])}, median {medianOf([a, b, c, d, e])}

questions.prompt: Find the mode of these marks: {listStr([a, b, c, d, e])}.

misconceptions.explain: That is the median; the mode is the most frequent value.
misconceptions.when: medianOf([a, b, c, d, e]) != modeOf([a, b, c, d, e])

solution: Count how often each value appears.
